title: Five in the Morning
subtitle: Emma starts work before the city wakes up. This is her day, hour by hour.
description: An A1 reading and listening text about times of day and the 12-hour clock, told through one woman's working day in Chicago.
source: authored for this site; no source document
passage: I start work early. The coffee shop opens at six in the morning, so I get up at five.
I don't like five o'clock. But I get up, I take a shower, and I make coffee at home. Jack is still in bed. He works from home, and he starts at nine.
I leave the apartment at half past five. The bus comes at 5:40 and takes twenty minutes.
The first hour is quiet. Then, at seven, the shop is busy. Everybody wants coffee before work, and from seven to ten I don't stop.
I have lunch at half past twelve, but only for thirty minutes. I finish at two in the afternoon and I am home at three.
Jack finishes at six. We have dinner together at seven, and I go to bed at ten. Tomorrow I get up at five again.

vocabulary.definition: to leave your bed in the morning
to wash your body under water
to go away from a place
to need an amount of time
with a lot of work or a lot of people
to end; to stop doing something

exercises.title: Understanding the Text
exercises.instructions: Read again and choose the best answer.

items.prompt: Why does Emma get up at five?
options: Because her work opens very early
items.explanation: The coffee shop opens at six, so she has to get up at five.

items.prompt: What is Jack doing when Emma gets up?
items.explanation: “Jack is still in bed” — he is not up yet.

items.prompt: How does Emma go to work?

options: In the first hour, from six to seven
items.explanation: “The first hour is quiet. Then, at seven, the shop is busy.”
“only for thirty minutes” — thirty minutes is half an hour.

items.prompt: Who finishes work later, Emma or Jack?
options: Jack. He finishes at six and she finishes at two
They finish at the same time
items.explanation: Emma finishes at two in the afternoon; Jack finishes at six.

exercises.title: Times and Days
exercises.instructions: Complete each sentence with one word.

items.prompt: I ___ ___ at five o'clock every morning.
items.explanation: To get up is to leave your bed.

items.prompt: The shop is ___ from seven to ten. A lot of people come in.
items.explanation: Busy means with a lot of people or work.

items.prompt: At six in the morning the street is ___. Nobody is there.

items.explanation: Half past seven is thirty minutes after seven.

items.prompt: The bus ___ twenty minutes to the city.
items.explanation: We use take for an amount of time.

items.prompt: It's nine o'clock and Jack is ___ in bed.
items.explanation: Still means it is continuing now.
True. She gets up at five; he is still in bed.

items.statement: Emma works in the afternoon and at night.
items.explanation: False. She finishes at two in the afternoon.

items.statement: Jack goes to an office every day.
Emma and Jack eat dinner at the same time.
items.explanation: True. “We have dinner together at seven.”

discussion: What time do you get up?
What time do you start and finish work?
Is the morning quiet or busy where you live?
What do you do before you go to bed?
